children: Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 16, 2026) - Silverco Mining Ltd.

(OTCQB: SICOF) ("Silverco" or the "Company") is pleased to provide an update on the restart of its 100% owned Cusi Property ("Cusi") in Chihuahua, Mexico. First concentrate was shipped from the project on schedule, and restart capital remains on budget.
Mark Ayranto, CEO of Silverco, commented:

"Shipping first concentrate from Cusi is a defining milestone for Silverco and delivers on the commitment we made to shareholders to restart Cusi in Q4 2026. From our first underground blast to the refurbishment of the Mal Paso plant, our team executed this restart on schedule and on budget, and importantly, did so safely. With operations at Cusi restarted, Silverco now has two operating silver mines in Mexico, a significant catalyst that diversifies our production base and cash flow. I want to thank our employees, contractors, and other stakeholders for their hard work and support in reaching this significant milestone.

"Our focus now turns to finalizing commissioning and ramping up Cusi to 1,200 tonnes per day and finalizing capital investments and operational improvements at La Negra to declare commercial production at both projects in H1 2027. Combined, based on recent technical reports
, Cusi and La Negra are positioned to deliver more than 4 million ounces of silver equivalent production in 2027."
Restart Highlights
First Concentrate Shipped, On Budget and Schedule —

The first concentrate shipment from Cusi was shipped today, on budget and schedule. Production rates and grades are scheduled to increase through H1 2027 as underground development ramps up, to reach design capacity of 1,200 tpd.
Cusi Management Team Buildout Complete —

A total of 142 employees and 246 contractors are currently active at Cusi, with all key hires in place. The team benefits from senior personnel with extensive experience in underground operations in Mexico.
Underground Development —

Underground development continues, and with the Mal Paso plant now operational, the focus has shifted to ramping up development rates. Ore level development is ongoing at Promontorio, and the ramp decline at San Miguel is progressing. Initial stope production is planned for late Q4 2026 in Promontorio.
Mal Paso Plant —

Refurbishment of the Mal Paso plant is nearing completion with dry commissioning now complete and wet commissioning substantially complete. Minor adjustments over the month are expected, and full operational handover is planned for the end of November. The only remaining elements requiring completion are installation of the tailings thickener, which is under construction and will be completed in January 2027. The thickener is not required for operations.
A Strong Safety Record —
Incurred one lost time incident ("LTI") across 577,000 exposure hours worked by Silverco and contractor personnel at Cusi to date in 2026.
Exploration Identifying Opportunities Within Planned Mine Footprint:
2026 drill results (see
, and

news releases) from the Company's 30,000 m program have reinforced the potential to define additional mineralization within or close to the planned mine footprint at Cusi. This presents an opportunity to enhance the mine plan early in the restart. Drilling is ongoing and is also targeting the high potential San Miguel deposit and San Juan target, with an updated mineral resource estimate planned for H1 2027.

Planned Cusi Restart

As outlined in an April 13, 2026 news release, the Cusi project offers compelling economics based on the results from the 2026 PEA2 which outlined a project with average annual silver equivalent production of approximately 2.5 Moz with an all-in-sustaining cost of US$26.75/oz payable AgEq from 2028 to 2032. In addition to Cusi providing very near-term cash flow, the ongoing exploration program has the potential to significantly enhance project economics early in the mine life. With 90% of the revenue generated from silver and low upfront capital of US$19.2 million, Cusi represents a unique near-term opportunity for Silverco to advance its vision of becoming a 10 million ounce per year silver equivalent producer within three years.

About Silverco Mining Ltd.

Silverco Mining Ltd. is a Canadian silver producer focused on building a leading multi-asset silver portfolio in Mexico. The Company owns 100% of the producing La Negra Mine in Querétaro and the past-producing Cusi Silver Complex in Chihuahua, two established underground mining operations with significant infrastructure, exploration upside, and district-scale land positions. The Company is restarting Cusi in H2 2026, positioning Silverco to become a significant primary silver producer in the Americas in the near term.

Led by an experienced management team with a proven track record in mine development, operations, and capital markets, Silverco is focused on creating long-term shareholder value through disciplined growth and responsible mining practices, with a goal of becoming a 10-million-ounce per year silver equivalent producer within three years. Silverco's common shares trade on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol "SICO" and on the OTCQB under the symbol "SICOF". More information on the Company and its projects can be found at www.silvercomining.com.
